note.question: Which mix of fines and public investment can enforce data portability without driving smaller data controllers out or reinforcing dominant firms?
note.overview: A policy-maker first sets fixed and revenue-based fines and invests in portability infrastructure. Heterogeneous data controllers then strategically choose participation, compliance, and Cournot output. The paper derives stage-2 Nash output, endogenous compliance and entry thresholds, and the equilibrium effects of each policy instrument.

source.quote: Braulin and Valletti (2016) consider the exclusivity of data sales by a monopolist data broker to two competing retailers and find that the data broker sells data exclusively to either the high-quality or the low-quality retailer.

For instance, Gal-Or et al. (2018) model firms that have different targeting capabilities, Cho et al. (2016) model firms that differ in the revenue rate per unit of content, and Mei et al. (2022) model firms that differ in their ARPU.
The structure of our assumptions is related to Nault and Zimmermann (2019), where DC (edge provider in their model) costs and profits change with decisions made in earlier stages.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: Stage 1: the policy-maker chooses fixed fines F, revenue-proportional fines f, and investment I that lowers compliance costs. Stage 2: data controllers decide whether to participate and, conditional on participation, whether to comply. Each compliance option embeds an optimal output choice; the controllers' simultaneous output best responses form the generalized Cournot Nash equilibrium used in the compliance and participation comparisons. Profits, user surplus, controller surplus, and policy costs are then realized.

components.label: Solution or estimation method
components.explanation: The paper keeps demand and cost functions general under monotonicity, curvature, and single-crossing assumptions. It solves compliant and noncompliant quantity choices, derives endogenous compliance and participation thresholds, applies comparative statics to fixed fines, variable fines, and investment, and aggregates equilibrium output and profit to study concentration and welfare.

components.label: Generalized Cournot-Nash output equilibrium with endogenous compliance and participation cutoffs
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Generalized Cournot-Nash output equilibrium with endogenous compliance and participation cutoffs. For any observed stage-1 instruments and compliance profile, Equations (4) and (7) jointly determine all controllers' best-response output and the paper explicitly identifies their combination as a Nash equilibrium. Profit comparisons then determine the compliance cutoff and zero-profit conditions determine entry, completing the stage-2 equilibrium used for policy comparative statics.
